problem: toLocalDateString returns a UTC date when NODE_ENV === 'test'. The production branch (getFullYear/getMonth/getDate, lines 12-15) is therefore never executed by any Vitest run. This function feeds the daily-challenge streak (lib/daily-challenges.ts:38,134), the daily seed (lib/seeded.ts:9) and daily-myth (lib/daily-myth.ts:9).
impact: The previous audit's TIME-001 (UTC day rollover) fix is the exact code that no test exercises. A regression back to UTC, or a bug in the local branch, passes CI and breaks streaks and the daily myth near local midnight for non-UTC readers.
fix: Remove the test-env branch. Pin the timezone in tests (process.env.TZ in vitest globalSetup, or vi.setSystemTime plus a fixed TZ) and update the UTC-based fixtures. Add cases for a date at 23:30 in America/Los_Angeles and 00:30 in Pacific/Auckland.
verification: rg -n 'NODE_ENV' apps/web/src/lib/date.ts shows the branch; pnpm --filter web exec vitest run src/__tests__/lib/daily-challenges.test.ts with TZ=Pacific/Auckland must pass without the branch.
resolution: #284: test-only UTC branch removed, vitest pins TZ=UTC, UTC+14 test fails on old code

problem: CSP violation reports are acknowledged with 204 and discarded (the file comment calls itself a stub). Separately, if csp-manifest.json fails to load, proxy.ts falls back to a policy with 'unsafe-inline', logging once. Nothing alerts on either condition.
impact: A deploy that ships a broken or missing hash manifest silently weakens script-src on every prerendered page, and real violations (or an XSS attempt blocked by CSP) are never seen. Mitigated: /csp-manifest.json is served 200 in production (curl 2026-11-04), so the degraded mode is not active today.
fix: Forward reports to Sentry (or log at warn with a sampled counter) in the route, with a body size cap. Add a post-deploy smoke check that asserts the live response header does not carry x-csp-mode: degraded.
verification: curl -sI https://mythosatlas.com/ | grep -i x-csp-mode returns nothing today; the check should fail a deploy when present.

problem: The proxy matcher excludes only a few named files, so every other file in public/ (images, 26 MB of audio, svg) runs through the proxy. Measured on production: /audio/stories/ramayana.mp3 (1.29 MB), /pantheons/greek.jpg (1.07 MB) and /favicon.svg each return a per-request CSP header with a fresh nonce and a Set-Cookie: locale, and Cache-Control: public, max-age=0, must-revalidate. No headers() rule sets longer cache lifetimes for them.
impact: Each static asset request invokes the proxy and makes the browser revalidate on every visit. Wasted proxy invocations and extra round trips, and a cookie plus CSP header on binary files that cannot use them. Edge caching still returns HIT (x-vercel-cache), so cost is latency and invocation count, not correctness.
fix: Add extensions (png|jpe?g|webp|avif|svg|mp3|woff2) or the public asset directories (audio, pantheons, deities, creatures, artifacts, heroes, locations, icons) to the matcher exclusion list. Add a headers() entry such as Cache-Control public, max-age=86400, stale-while-revalidate=604800 for those paths (immutable only if filenames are content-hashed).
verification: curl -sI https://mythosatlas.com/pantheons/greek.jpg | grep -i -E 'cache-control|set-cookie|content-security' should show a long max-age and no cookie or CSP after the change.
resolution: PR #289 merged b988e108, CI green incl. E2E + visual. Proxy matcher skips static asset extensions; static files get a locked-down CSP from next.config headers (security review follow-up).

problem: The PostHog relay is unauthenticated and streams request.body upstream with no size cap, no rate limit, no AbortSignal timeout, and no try/catch around fetch(upstreamUrl, init). Only an allowlist of SDK paths is reachable, and cookies are not forwarded (good).
impact: An upstream outage or a slow client holds a serverless function open until the platform timeout and surfaces as an unhandled 500. Anyone can push large bodies through the site's function quota. Blast radius is limited to the allowlisted PostHog paths.
fix: Reject requests whose content-length exceeds a small cap (for example 512 KB), pass AbortSignal.timeout(5000), wrap the fetch in try/catch returning 502, and apply the existing Upstash rate limiter used for newsletter/oracle.
verification: Unit-test the route with a mocked rejecting fetch: expect 502, not an unhandled throw. rg -n 'try|signal' apps/web/src/app/ingest returns nothing today.
resolution: PR #289 merged b988e108, CI green incl. E2E + visual. /ingest counts real body bytes (413 past 512 KB, chunked or understated length included), 5 s upstream timeout, 502 on failure.

problem: Quiz option order uses .sort(() => Math.random() - 0.5), a biased shuffle (inconsistent comparator, engine-dependent). Correct Fisher-Yates shuffleArray already exists twice (lib/relationship-quiz.ts:54, components/games/SymbolMemoryGame.tsx:154) and is not shared.
impact: Correct-answer position is statistically non-uniform in the main quiz, so answers are slightly guessable. Three copies of shuffle logic exist; two are right and one pattern is wrong.
fix: Extract one shuffle helper into lib/ (move relationship-quiz's), switch MythologyQuiz, QuickQuizPageClient and SymbolMemoryGame to it. Refactor commit first, behaviour change second.
verification: rg -n 'Math.random\(\) - 0.5' apps/web/src returns no matches after the change; add a test that shuffles [1,2,3] 10000 times with a seeded RNG and checks each permutation within tolerance.

problem: The learning backup covers 4 keys (bookmarks, reading-progress, progress, review). Interactive-story progress and discovered endings (mythos-story-progress, mythos-story-endings) live in localStorage but are not exported or restored.
impact: A reader who restores a backup on a new device loses story endings they discovered, while the UI presents the backup as their learning data. Silent partial restore.
fix: Either add the two story keys to LEARNING_STORAGE_KEYS (bump LEARNING_BACKUP_VERSION, validate with Zod like the others) or state in the Backup UI copy what is excluded.
verification: Export, clear storage, import: story endings must reappear. rg -n 'mythos-story' apps/web/src/lib/learning-backup.ts is empty today.

problem: The coverage gate names progress-provider but not bookmarks-provider or review-provider, although both parse and persist user data to localStorage (bookmarks-provider.tsx:61,88; review-provider.tsx:81).
impact: Regressions in persistence or migration of bookmarks and spaced-repetition state are not caught by the 62/64 percent aggregate or the per-module 80 percent gates.
fix: Add both providers to the coverage include list with the same 80/80/80/70 thresholds as progress-provider, and add tests for corrupt JSON and quota-exceeded writes.
verification: pnpm --filter web test:coverage output lists both files with thresholds.
resolution: #284: bookmarks- and review-provider gated with per-file floors under measured coverage

problem: About 14 dependency pins are duplicated between the root and apps/web package.json. msw and vite appear unused and are hidden by knip.json ignoreDependencies, so the knip CI gate cannot flag them.
impact: Two places to bump per upgrade (Dependabot limit settings amplify drift), and dead dependencies stay in the lockfile and supply-chain surface.
fix: Keep shared tooling at the root only, or move to a pnpm catalog. Confirm msw/vite usage with rg, then remove them and their knip ignore entries.
verification: rg -n "from 'msw'|from 'vite'" apps/web returns nothing; pnpm knip passes after removing the ignore entries.
resolution: PR #289 merged b988e108, CI green incl. E2E + visual. msw removed. vite kept (peer + override). Duplicated pins not touched.

problem: The public /changelog page is hand-curated and was last updated at v1.13.1. Releases 1.14.0, 1.15.0 and 1.15.1 are tagged and in CHANGELOG.md but absent from the page. release-please does not touch changelog.json.
impact: Readers see a changelog three releases behind. Low user harm because curation is deliberate, but it will drift again.
fix: Backfill 1.14.0 to 1.15.1, or add a CI check that the newest tag appears in changelog.json (or label the page 'highlights').
verification: node -e "console.log(require('./apps/web/src/data/changelog.json')[0].version)" prints 1.13.1; git tag --sort=-v:refname | head -1 prints v1.15.1.

problem: footer.tsx (a server component) renders new Date().getFullYear() and not-found.tsx picks suggestions by Math.floor(Date.now() / 3600000). On a statically prerendered page both values freeze at build time.
impact: Copyright year will read the build year until the next deploy; the 'hourly' suggestion rotation is really per-deploy. Cosmetic.
fix: Compute the year in a tiny client component or accept per-deploy rotation and drop the 'hourly' comment/claim.
verification: Compare the footer year in the HTML of a page against the build date after a year boundary; or grep the prerendered .next/server/app output for the year string.
